title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Six Provisions on Judicial Openness and the Several Provisions on People's Courts Accepting Supervision by News Media and Public Opinion
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Six Provisions on Judicial Openness" and the "Several Provisions on People's Courts Accepting Supervision by News Media and Public Opinion"

Fa Fa [2009] No. 58

To all local people's courts at various levels nationwide, all military courts, all railway transport intermediate courts and basic courts, all maritime courts, and all courts of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The Supreme People's Court's "Six Provisions on Judicial Openness" and the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on People's Courts Accepting Supervision by News Media and Public Opinion" have been approved by the Central Committee. They are hereby issued to you for diligent implementation. In the course of implementation, any major matters shall be promptly reported to this Court.

December 8, 2009

Six Provisions on Judicial Openness

To further implement the constitutional principle of open trials, expand the scope of judicial openness, broaden the channels for judicial openness, safeguard the people's right to know, participate, express, and supervise the work of the people's courts, protect the lawful rights and interests of the parties, enhance the level of judicial democracy, standardize judicial conduct, and promote judicial fairness, these provisions are formulated in accordance with the provisions of relevant procedural laws and the actual work of the people's courts, and under the principles of openness according to law, timely openness, and comprehensive openness.

I. Openness in Case Filing

Information related to the case filing stage shall be disclosed to the parties through convenient and effective means. Contents such as the conditions for filing various types of cases, filing procedures, formats of legal documents, standards for litigation costs, procedures for deferring, reducing, or exempting litigation costs, the parties' significant rights and obligations, litigation and enforcement risk warnings, and available alternative dispute resolution methods shall be disclosed to the public and the parties through appropriate forms. The people's court shall promptly notify the parties of the acceptance of the case. If a case is not accepted, the people's court shall, in accordance with the law, promptly serve the relevant legal documents such as the ruling of non-acceptance, the notice of non-acceptance of a retrial application, or the ruling dismissing the retrial application, and shall explain the reasons and inform the parties of their litigation rights.

II. Openness in Court Hearings

Establish and improve rules for orderly open and effectively managed attendance and reporting of trials, eliminating obstacles to public and media oversight. For cases heard openly in accordance with the law, attendees shall undergo security checks before entering the courtroom. Where objective factors such as trial venue capacity are limited, the people's court may distribute attendance passes or use trial videos, live broadcasts, or recordings to meet the need of the public and media to understand the actual trial proceedings. All evidence shall be disclosed in court, and if it can be authenticated in court, it shall be authenticated in court. Except for circumstances where witnesses or expert evaluators are not required to appear in court as stipulated by law or judicial interpretations, the people's court shall notify witnesses and expert evaluators to testify in court. The basic information of the sole adjudicator, members of the collegial panel, and members of the adjudication committee shall be disclosed, and the parties have the right to apply for withdrawal in accordance with the law. The parties shall be informed of any extension of the trial period. For cases tried either openly or in camera, the people's court shall publicly announce the judgment in the courtroom or through other public means.

III. Openness in Enforcement

The basis, standards, rules, procedures, and the entire process of enforcement shall be disclosed to the public and the parties, except for information prohibited by law from disclosure, such as state secrets, trade secrets, or personal privacy. Further improve and perfect the enforcement information inquiry system, expand the scope of inquiries, and facilitate parties' access to information on enforcement cases. After taking enforcement measures such as sealing, distraining, freezing, or transferring funds, the people's court shall promptly inform both parties. The process and results of the selection of institutions for appraisal, evaluation, or auction by the people's court shall be disclosed to the parties. Key aspects and major matters, such as the collection and distribution of enforcement funds, the custody, evaluation, auction, or sale of the subject matter of enforcement, and their procedures and results, shall be promptly informed to the parties. Any significant progress in enforcement shall be notified to the parties and interested parties.

IV. Openness in Hearings

Where a people's court holds hearings on cases involving significant rights and interests of the parties or third parties outside the trial proceedings, such hearings shall be conducted openly. For cases involving retrial applications, difficult petitions in litigation-related or law-related cases, judicial compensation cases, enforcement objection cases, and cases of commutation or parole for defendants in duty crimes or cases with significant impact, if the people's court conducts open hearings in accordance with relevant provisions, it shall issue a public notice of the hearing. The scope, methods, and procedures for open hearings shall, insofar as applicable, follow the relevant provisions on open trials.

V. Openness of Documents

Judgment documents shall fully set forth the parties' allegations and defenses, the reasons for admitting evidence, the establishment of facts, and the reasoning and interpretation process for the application of law, achieving openness in reasoning. The people's court may, as needed for legal education, legal research, case guidance, and uniform judgment standards, systematically compile and publish various types of judgment documents. Except for cases involving state secrets, juvenile crimes, personal privacy, or other cases unsuitable for publication, as well as cases concluded by mediation, the people's court's judgment documents may be publicly released on the internet. If a party raises an objection to the public release of a judgment document on the internet and has justifiable reasons, the people's court may decide not to release it on the internet. To protect the legitimate rights of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations involved in the judgment documents, necessary technical processing may be applied to relevant information in the judgment documents to be publicly released. The people's court shall pay attention to collecting opinions and suggestions from all sectors of society regarding judgment documents for reference in improving work.

VI. Openness of Court Affairs

The people's court's trial management work and other management activities related to trial work shall be open to the public. People's courts at all levels shall gradually establish and improve internet websites and other information disclosure platforms. Explore the establishment of online inquiry systems for the processing procedures of various types of cases, facilitating parties' timely inquiry into case progress. Through convenient and effective means, promptly disclose to the public policies on court work, various normative documents and trial guidance opinions, non-confidential judicial statistics and analysis reports, and disclose the trial situation of major cases, important research findings, activity deployments, etc. Establish and improve systems for registering inquiries about cases, warnings against interference through influence, and reporting on supervision situations, disclosing to the public and the parties situations where cases are inquired about in violation of procedural rules and the circumstances under which the people's court accepts supervision, effectively protecting the public's right to know and supervise and the parties' litigation rights.

People's courts at all levels nationwide shall practically emancipate their minds, update their concepts, boldly innovate, combine proactive adoption of transparent measures with the full realization of the parties' litigation rights, and regard the degree of judicial openness as an important indicator for measuring the level of judicial democracy and evaluating court work. The Supreme People's Court will further study and formulate evaluation standards for the implementation of the judicial openness system, incorporate them into the evaluation system for people's court work, and improve the assessment and evaluation mechanism for judicial openness. Higher-level people's courts shall strengthen guidance on judicial openness work of lower-level people's courts, regularly organize special inspections, announce inspection results, and improve the supervision and inspection mechanism for judicial openness. People's courts at all levels shall increase investment in funding, facilities, human resources, and technology for judicial openness work, and establish a material safeguard mechanism for judicial openness. They shall unblock channels, establish platforms, seriously collect, listen to, and handle public reports, complaints, or opinions and suggestions regarding the implementation of the judicial openness system, and establish and improve a feedback mechanism for judicial openness situations. They shall refine and decompose the responsibilities for judicial openness, clarify responsibilities, and hold accountable those who, in the course of proceedings, violate the principle of open trial or, in other court work, violate relevant provisions on judicial openness. At the same time, attention shall be paid to establishing advanced models, commending advanced individuals and units, and promoting advanced experiences, in order to establish and improve the accountability and commendation mechanism for judicial openness.

These provisions shall take effect on the date of their publication. Where any previous provisions issued by this Court are inconsistent with these provisions, these provisions shall prevail.

Several Provisions on People's Courts Accepting Supervision by News Media and Public Opinion

To further implement the constitutional principle of open trials, standardize the work of people's courts in accepting supervision by news media and public opinion, properly handle the relationship between courts and the media, safeguard the public's right to know, participate, express, and supervise, and enhance judicial credibility, these provisions are formulated.

Article 1: People's courts shall actively accept supervision by news media and public opinion. When news media request to attend court hearings, interview or report on court work, or request the provision of relevant materials, the people's court shall provide convenience according to the specific circumstances.

Article 2: With respect to cases of social concern, major measures in court work, and other information that should be disclosed to the public in accordance with relevant regulations, the people's court shall promptly release relevant information to the news media through press conferences, press briefings, press releases, court gazettes, internet websites, and other forms.

Article 3: For cases tried in open court, journalists and the public may attend as observers. If there are insufficient seats in the courtroom, priority shall be given to meeting the needs of the media and close relatives of the parties. Where conditions permit, courtrooms may set up a media section in the observer area. Journalists attending trials shall comply with courtroom discipline and shall not record audio, video, or take photographs without authorization.

Article 4: For cases currently under trial, adjudicators and other staff of the people's court shall not accept interviews by the news media without authorization. For cases already concluded, the people's court may, through coordination by the news and publicity department, decide to have relevant personnel accept interviews. If an interview is deemed unsuitable, the people's court may decide not to accept the interview and shall explain the reasons.

Article 5: When news media require the people's court to provide relevant materials for reporting on trial situations or other court work, the people's court may provide copies of judgment documents, trial transcripts, audio and video recordings of trials, normative documents, and guidance opinions. If necessary, other publicly available background materials and explanations of circumstances may also be provided to the media.

Article 6: The coordination work of people's courts accepting supervision by news media and public opinion shall be managed under a unified system by the news and publicity departments of people's courts at all levels. The news and publicity departments shall provide news reporting materials to the news media, ensuring that news media report on the work of the people's courts truthfully and objectively. When news media report on the work of the people's courts inaccurately, the news and publicity department shall be responsible for promptly clarifying the facts and responding.

Article 7: People's courts shall establish fixed communication and liaison mechanisms with news media and their supervisory departments, regularly or irregularly hold symposiums or seminars to exchange opinions and share information. People's courts and news media may study and formulate mutual codes of conduct. For opinions and suggestions reflected by the news media regarding the people's court's acceptance of supervision by public opinion, the relevant court shall promptly study and handle them, and improve its work.

Article 8: With respect to problems in the trial work and other work of the people's courts reflected in news media reports, as well as reports of illegal or disciplinary conduct by adjudicators or other staff, the people's court shall promptly investigate and verify. If verified, effective measures shall be taken in accordance with the law to address the situation, and the results of the handling shall be promptly communicated back.

Article 9: Where a people's court discovers that news media, in the course of interviewing and reporting on court work, engage in any of the following circumstances, it may report the situation to the competent news authorities, the self-regulatory organization of journalists, or the news organization, and make suggestions. If it violates the law, corresponding legal liability shall be pursued.

(1) Harming national security and public interests, disclosing state secrets or trade secrets;

(2) Reporting on cases currently under trial with serious inaccuracy or maliciously engaging in biased reporting, thereby damaging judicial authority or affecting fair trial;

(3) Damaging the reputation of judges through insults, defamation, or other means, or damaging the right to reputation or other personality rights of parties, or infringing on the privacy and safety of litigation participants;

(4) Accepting entrustment from one party, distorting facts, maliciously stirring up publicity, interfering with the trial or enforcement activities of the people's court, causing serious adverse effects;

(5) Other acts that seriously damage judicial authority or affect judicial fairness.

Article 10: These provisions shall take effect on the date of their publication.
